package_info.why_malicious: This package version contains multiple high and medium severity vulnerabilities, including arbitrary code execution, remote code execution, access control bypass, arbitrary file upload, cross-site scripting (XSS), and denial of service (DoS). These vulnerabilities enable attackers to execute malicious code, bypass security restrictions, compromise user sessions, and disrupt service availability. While not intentionally malicious, the presence of these vulnerabilities exposes production systems to severe exploitation risks.

execution_context.file_location: core Drupal PHP files responsible for file upload handling (e.g., includes/file.inc, modules/file/file.module)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Vulnerable input handling in file upload functionality, allowing arbitrary file upload (see https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PHP-DRUPALDRUPAL-538568)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the file upload handler processes user-supplied files without sufficient validation, allowing attackers to upload arbitrary files (including executable PHP scripts), which are then placed in web-accessible directories, resulting in remote code execution when accessed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Permitting uploads of arbitrary files, especially executable scripts, is a critical security flaw that enables attackers to deploy web shells or other malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: File upload handlers are expected to strictly validate file types, extensions, and content, and to prevent placement of executable files in web-accessible locations. The vulnerable code omits these controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate file upload features exist but must enforce strict validation and sanitization to prevent code execution.
key_indicators: Absence of file type/content validation in upload logic
Acceptance of files with .php or other executable extensions
Placement of uploaded files in directories accessible via the web server

execution_context.file_location: core Drupal PHP files handling user input and dynamic execution paths (e.g., includes/bootstrap.inc, modules/system/system.module)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Improper input validation leading to arbitrary code execution (see https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PHP-DRUPALDRUPAL-174350 and https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PHP-DRUPALDRUPAL-1048286)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes user-supplied input without adequate sanitization and passes it to dynamic execution functions (such as eval()), enabling attackers to inject and execute arbitrary PHP code on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing user input to reach dynamic execution functions like eval() is a severe vulnerability, as it gives attackers direct control over server-side code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: User input should always be sanitized and never directly executed. The vulnerable code path allows unsanitized input to be evaluated as code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic code execution is only legitimate in tightly controlled plugin systems with strict validation, not in general input handling.
key_indicators: Use of eval(), create_function(), or similar on user input
Lack of input sanitization or validation before execution
Ability to inject PHP code via request parameters

execution_context.file_location: core Drupal PHP files implementing access control logic (e.g., modules/user/user.module, includes/menu.inc)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Access control bypass due to improper permission checks (see https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PHP-DRUPALDRUPAL-174352 and https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PHP-DRUPALDRUPAL-70088)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the access control logic fails to enforce proper permission checks, allowing unauthorized users to access or modify restricted resources and perform privileged actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bypassing access controls enables privilege escalation and unauthorized access to sensitive data or administrative functions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Access control mechanisms must strictly enforce user permissions. The vulnerable code allows actions without verifying user roles or privileges.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for bypassing access controls; all access to restricted resources must be properly authorized.
key_indicators: Missing or incorrect permission checks in access control logic
Non-privileged users able to access or modify admin-only resources
Absence of role or capability verification before sensitive actions

execution_context.file_location: core Drupal PHP files responsible for input/output handling and rendering (e.g., includes/theme.inc, modules/system/system.module)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Cross-site scripting (XSS) due to improper output encoding (see https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PHP-DRUPALDRUPAL-174348)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code outputs user-supplied data directly into HTML responses without proper encoding, allowing attackers to inject malicious JavaScript that executes in the browsers of other users.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: XSS vulnerabilities allow attackers to hijack user sessions, steal cookies, or perform actions as other users by injecting malicious scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: All user input should be properly encoded (e.g., using htmlspecialchars()) before being rendered in HTML. The vulnerable code fails to apply output encoding.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason to output raw user input in HTML without encoding.
key_indicators: Direct insertion of user input into HTML output
Lack of output encoding functions such as htmlspecialchars() or htmlentities()
Ability to inject and execute JavaScript via user-supplied data

execution_context.file_location: core Drupal PHP files managing resource-intensive operations (e.g., modules/system/system.module, includes/common.inc)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion (see https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PHP-DRUPALDRUPAL-538570)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code allows attackers to trigger resource-intensive operations (such as large file uploads or complex queries) without proper input validation or rate limiting, leading to server resource exhaustion and service unavailability.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unrestricted resource consumption can be exploited to degrade or deny service to legitimate users, constituting a DoS attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Resource-intensive operations should be protected by input validation, quotas, and rate limiting. The vulnerable code lacks these safeguards.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate resource usage must always be controlled to prevent abuse.
key_indicators: No input validation on resource-consuming endpoints
Absence of rate limiting or quotas for expensive operations
Ability to trigger high CPU/memory usage via crafted requests

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads a malicious file (e.g., PHP web shell) via the vulnerable file upload handler.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious file is stored on the server in a web-accessible directory.

attack_chain.action: Attacker accesses the uploaded file, triggering remote code execution on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains arbitrary code execution capabilities on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits access control bypass to escalate privileges or access restricted resources.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can perform unauthorized actions or access sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript via XSS to compromise other users' sessions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can steal session cookies or perform actions as other users.

attack_chain.action: Attacker triggers resource exhaustion to cause denial of service.
attack_chain.leads_to: Service becomes unavailable to legitimate users.

behavioral_signatures: File upload endpoints accepting executable files (e.g., .php) without validation
Use of eval(), create_function(), or similar functions on user-supplied input
Access to admin or restricted resources by non-privileged users
Direct output of user input in HTML responses without encoding
Unusually high resource consumption or repeated expensive operations from a single user or endpoint
file_indicators: Unexpected .php files in upload directories (e.g., sites/default/files/)
Files with executable permissions in web-accessible locations
network_indicators: Outbound connections initiated by uploaded files or web shells
Unusual HTTP requests to admin endpoints from non-admin users
Repeated large POST requests or requests triggering resource-intensive operations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor file upload endpoints for acceptance of executable files and scan upload directories (e.g., sites/default/files/) for unexpected .php files. Audit code for use of eval(), create_function(), or similar functions on user input. Implement logging and alerting for access control violations, such as non-admin users accessing admin endpoints. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to detect and block XSS payloads, and monitor for abnormal resource usage patterns or repeated expensive operations indicative of DoS attacks.
